angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 6,779,596 km at 52.03 pc = 1.74 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14838: distance 52.029 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.01), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 52.029 +/- 0.52 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 19.7731 +/- 0.1592 mas (same row, RUWE 1.89), 124.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 9.745 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14838: radius 9.745 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 50.038 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.052) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 6,779,596 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4921 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14838: effective temperature 4921 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.056) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14838: effective temperature 4921 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.056) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * del Ari: spectral type G9.5IIIb (1989ApJS...71..245K)
luminositySource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 60248877811546112, flags_flame 10: lum_flame 52.682194 solar luminosities (16th to 84th percentiles 51.8743 to 53.492752); its log10 is recorded

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 19787) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
